title: The Friendship Formula
coreMove: Diagnose a relationship by separating proximity, frequency, duration, and intensity before deciding what to strengthen or reduce.
sourcePressure: The source sidecar frames friendship as a four-part model: proximity, frequency, duration, and intensity. It stresses nonthreatening proximity, intensity as emotional glue, and the ethical edge that the same levers can deepen unhealthy influence.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating the formula as a magic closeness recipe or assuming more contact always improves a bond.

sourceAnchors.name: Friendship = Proximity x (Frequency + Duration) x Intensity
sourceAnchors.detail: The ch01 source sidecar names this formula as the central required anchor and treats intensity as the glue that gives the other variables force.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The formula is useful because it makes a vague bond visible: you can see whether the missing piece is access, repetition, time, or emotional weight.

sourceAnchors.name: nonthreatening proximity
sourceAnchors.detail: The ch01 sidecar says proximity matters only when exposure happens in a setting that does not feel threatening.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Standing near someone does not help if the room makes them brace; safety is what lets proximity begin to count.

counterintuition: more time always means more closeness
relationships are not luck, they are math
tryThisNow: set a timer and think of a friend
text someone right now without diagnosing the missing variable

exampleSpecs.domain: a museum volunteer coordinator trying to revive a thin docent pairing
exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator who sees two capable volunteers never become a team
exampleSpecs.stakes: a tour launch will fail if they keep trading only logistics
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator moves the pair from rushed sign-in contact to a shared 20-minute object-handling prep and watches warmth appear only after intensity enters
exampleSpecs.firstImage: white cotton gloves beside a tray of Roman coins
mustAvoid: break-room small talk or generic team bonding

exampleSpecs.domain: a youth hockey assistant coach managing a quiet goalie and a new defender
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach who wants trust without forcing friendship
exampleSpecs.stakes: one blown tournament game could harden the pair into blame
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach changes short locker-room proximity into repeated five-minute post-drill reviews where the defender asks the goalie what he saw
exampleSpecs.firstImage: skate guards lined under a rink bench

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice volunteer lead pairing a new visitor with a guarded family caregiver
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer lead handling fragile trust
exampleSpecs.stakes: too much intensity too early could feel intrusive, too little will make visits useless
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: it takes three visits for the lead to see that shorter, steadier visits beat one long emotional first visit
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sign-in clipboard with three short visit notes

exampleSpecs.domain: a community theater stage manager blending two backstage crews
exampleSpecs.audience: a stage manager before opening night
exampleSpecs.stakes: missed cues will look like incompetence to the audience
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the stage manager stops counting rehearsal attendance as closeness and adds one shared cue-reset ritual that gives the contact intensity
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Reset from the blackout," Grace says into the headset

exampleSpecs.domain: a tenant association treasurer cooling an exhausting relationship with an overbearing member
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer treasurer who needs distance without a fight
exampleSpecs.stakes: the member is turning every repair email into a two-hour call
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the treasurer reviews which variable she fed by answering instantly and begins reducing frequency and duration without hostility
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What made one repair request become a nightly phone call?

exampleSpecs.domain: a rowing club captain integrating a shy novice into a crew
exampleSpecs.audience: a captain who mistakes shared practice for attachment
exampleSpecs.stakes: the novice may quit before regatta season starts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 6:12 a.m., Sarah predicts that shared water time is enough, then sees the novice bond only after a small recovery task carries emotional weight
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two oars resting on wet dock planks
mustAvoid: bike helmet, narrow kitchen, classroom desk

skillTargets: identify which of the four variables is missing in a stalled relationship
distinguish frequency from duration in concrete scenes
judge when intensity is unhealthy rather than bonding
choose how to cool a relationship by reducing variables without drama

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one real relationship and label the weakest variable in one sentence; choose one small adjustment that changes only that variable.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
